facts.claim: A container is an isolated process with its own filesystem, and an image is a package of everything a container needs to start.
Data stored in a volume persists after the container using it is removed.
The Windows page requires Windows 10 64-bit version 22H2 or Windows 11 64-bit version 23H2 or higher, in the Enterprise, Pro or Education editions.
The Windows page requires a 64-bit processor with SLAT, 8GB of system RAM and hardware virtualization enabled in BIOS/UEFI for the WSL 2 backend.
The Windows page requires WSL version 2.1.5 or later for the WSL 2 backend.
The Windows page says the per-user installation of Docker Desktop does not require administrator privileges.
The Mac page offers Docker Desktop for Mac for Apple silicon and for Intel chips.
The Mac page says Docker Desktop is supported on the current and two previous major macOS releases.
The Docker Engine install page lists supported Linux distributions, including Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora.
The Windows page says to double-click Docker Desktop Installer.exe, and that the Configuration page lets you choose the WSL 2 backend, which earlier versions label Use WSL 2 instead of Hyper-V.
The Windows page says that when the installation is successful you select Close to complete the installation.
The Windows page includes the command wsl --install, to be run in PowerShell or Windows Command Prompt in administrator mode, in its WSL install option.
The Mac page says to double-click Docker.dmg and drag the Docker icon to the Applications folder, where Docker Desktop is installed as Docker.app.
The Ubuntu page starts Docker with sudo systemctl start docker and verifies the installation by running the hello-world image.
The Debian page sets up the Docker apt repository before installing Docker Engine.
The Fedora page is one of the distribution install pages for Docker Engine.
The Docker Engine install page lists the supported Linux distributions and links to each distribution's install page.
The post-installation page says to add your user to the docker group with sudo usermod -aG docker $USER, then log out and log back in.
The post-installation page says the Docker daemon always runs as root, and other users can reach it only through sudo unless they are in the docker group.
The post-installation page says that on systemd distributions that do not start Docker on boot by default, sudo systemctl enable docker.service starts it.
The docker run command creates and runs a new container from an image.
The docker run command runs a command in a new container, pulling the image if needed and starting the container.
The docker ps command lists only running containers by default, and the --all flag includes stopped containers.
The docker ps reference describes the exited status as an integer representing the container's exit code.
The docker rm command removes one or more containers.
The Docker Desktop troubleshooting page describes how to diagnose and troubleshoot Docker Desktop and how to check the logs.
The docker logs reference describes the command as fetching the logs of a container.
The Nginx documentation is published on nginx.org under /en/docs/.
The Nginx download page describes a stable version and a mainline version.
The official Nginx image page on Docker Hub lists the stable tag.
The docker volume option ro mounts a volume into the container as read-only.
The PostgreSQL image page says POSTGRES_PASSWORD is the only environment variable the image requires.
The PostgreSQL image page says the PGDATA path is version-specific from PostgreSQL 18 on, and gives /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker for version 18.
The PostgreSQL versioning page lists version 17 as supported, with end of life on November 8, 2029.
The PostgreSQL documentation is published at postgresql.org/docs.
The official Node.js image page on Docker Hub lists node tags for the 24 release line.
The Node.js release schedule lists version 24 with the status LTS.
The Node.js HTTP module documentation describes http.createServer and server.listen.
Containers on the default bridge network can communicate using container IP addresses but cannot refer to each other by name.
On a user-defined network, containers can communicate with each other using container IP addresses or container names.
The default path for a Compose file is compose.yaml, which Compose prefers, and it is placed in the working directory.
When docker compose up runs, Compose creates a network named <project-name>_default and attaches all services to it, where each service is discoverable by its service name.
The docker compose down command removes named volumes declared in the volumes section of the Compose file when given the -v option.
Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container applications.
The Portainer Docker install page uses the image portainer/portainer-ce:lts and publishes port 9443.
The Portainer Docker install page mounts /var/run/docker.sock and the volume portainer_data to /data.
The Portainer install page says Portainer generates a self-signed SSL certificate for port 9443 by default.
The Portainer setup token FAQ says the setup token is found by searching the server logs for the line setup_token=.
The Portainer setup token FAQ says the administrator user must be created within 5 minutes.
The Portainer documentation index is at docs.portainer.io and covers version 2.45 LTS.
The Docker WSL page says that docker commands work from Windows without a WSL distribution installed.
The image portainer/portainer-ce is listed on Docker Hub.
The Dozzle getting started guide gives docker run with the socket mount, the dozzle_data volume, port 8080 and image amir20/dozzle:latest.
The Dozzle getting started guide says Dozzle needs Docker Engine 19.03 or newer and that it can be opened at localhost port 8080.
Docker Hub lists the amir20/dozzle image.
The Uptime Kuma site shows the run command with the louislam/uptime-kuma:2 image, port 3001 and the uptime-kuma volume.
Docker Hub lists version 2 tags for louislam/uptime-kuma.
The Adminer site gives the Docker command docker run -p 8080:8080 adminer and says Adminer supports PostgreSQL.
The Adminer site says Adminer does not allow connecting without a password, rate-limits connection attempts and should be kept inaccessible to the public.
Docker Hub has an image page for adminer.
The Nginx Proxy Manager guide shows a Compose file with image jc21/nginx-proxy-manager:2.17.1 and ports 80, 81 and 443.
The Nginx Proxy Manager guide says the tool can provide free SSL and that the admin interface is on port 81.
Docker Hub has an image page for jc21/nginx-proxy-manager.
pgAdmin's documentation includes a container deployment guide.
The Docker Desktop troubleshooting page describes how to diagnose and troubleshoot Docker Desktop and how to check the logs.
The post-installation page gives the commands sudo chown and sudo chmod for the .docker folder, and the newgrp docker command.
The docker system prune reference says it removes all unused containers, networks and images, including dangling images.
The Docker concepts guide describes what a container is.
Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container applications.
The Nginx documentation is published on nginx.org under /en/docs/.
The PostgreSQL documentation is published at postgresql.org/docs.
The Node.js documentation is published at nodejs.org under /en/docs.
